correctness.rationale: The published same-object Theorem 5.10 of Adams–Adetowubo–Barriga-Acosta–Feng–Sterling states nonequivariant K_k≈vee^(6k²-1)S² for k>=2, so only H0 and H2 occur rationally. A nonidentity translation preserving a simplex must have coordinate orders 1 or 3; nonzero entries in both coordinates yield orbit distance 2k>k. Exactly four axial translations ±(k,0), ±(0,k) remain; a fixed clique must be one three-point axial orbit triangle, of which 3k² exist, each orientation-preserving, giving Lefschetz L=3k². All other nonzero shifts fix no nonempty simplex, L=0; subtract trace H0=1. The resulting class function is the character of Q[G/Hx]+Q[G/Hy]-trivial, semisimple over Q, giving multiplicity 1_{3|u}+1_{3|v}-1_{(u,v)=0}; exactly one G-invariant line. Independent enumeration of all 888 faces and all 36 translations for k=2 yielded traces {23:1,11:4,-1:31}; the original verifier also checks k=3 and original Morse certificate covers only k=2. Infinite k uses the published theorem and a general orbit argument, not finite extrapolation.
